entries.answer: Keep

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: How old is he, and how long has he led the Black Guard?
entries.answer: Other (write my own)
entries.custom_text: He has always been in the military. He had his daughter at 30. His daughter is now 20. He started the black guard from scratch and the main character is under the first black guard division ever created.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: Which sin tempts him most (the bible says he is secretly very Proud)?
entries.answer: Other (write my own)
entries.custom_text: He looks humble and intelligent and smart and ambitious and humorous and just and caring and thinks what is best for the empire. Internally he is seeking the power that will save humanity and doesn’t believe the empire is doing it right. He was secretly born in a rival kingdom

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: How did he get the title?
entries.answer: Appointed by the Council for his brilliance

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: His view of the census of the corrupted?
entries.answer: Against it — he wants to use corruption, not count it

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: His role toward Alaric and Seraphina?
entries.answer: Other (write my own)
entries.custom_text: He mentors and truly sees Alaric as the future, but he will have to slowly change Alaric’s views to better the world. Truly loves his daughter but humanity comes first

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: Does Seraphina know Cassian was secretly born in a rival kingdom?
entries.answer: No, Seraphina doesn't know. She finds out during the story.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: Who was Seraphina's mother?
entries.answer: A noblewoman from the Capital Kingdom.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: Is Seraphina's mother still alive?
entries.answer: Yes. She is alive and still with Cassian.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: What role does Seraphina's mother play?
entries.answer: She is Cassian's conscience. She is not aware of his secrets.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: He was secretly born in a rival kingdom. Which one?
entries.answer: A south-east kingdom still at war with the Southern Kingdoms.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: What is the 'power that will save humanity' he is seeking?
entries.answer: He seeks a power tied to spirit-tech. He thinks it means a bargain with the fallen, but he doesn't fully know or understand who or what the fallen are.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: What does Cassian offer the fallen?
entries.answer: He doesn't fully know or understand who or what the fallen are, only that there is a power tied to spirit-tech.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: How does Cassian hope to use corruption?
entries.answer: To power spirit-tech.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: When does Alaric first notice Cassian quietly bending his views?
entries.answer: Alaric kind of falls into Cassian's ideology at first, but Seraphina talks it through with Alaric, and over time they both start to see something is off.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: Who knows Cassian was secretly born in a rival kingdom?
entries.answer: Nobody alive.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: What is the spirit-tech power Cassian is chasing?
entries.answer: All of the above: an ancient device that opens a crossing, powered by pulling energy out of corrupted things; the Flame Order forbade and hid it; Cassian doesn't know exactly what it is and follows rumors.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: How does Cassian's wife act as his conscience?
entries.answer: Her faith keeps him tied to the Flame Order's teachings.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: What is the south-east kingdom Cassian was born in called?
entries.answer: Dravenmoor (named by Story; Chumi may rename).

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: How does Cassian feel about the Flame Order being independent?
entries.answer: Cassian respects them publicly but resents them privately, sees them as an obstacle to his spirit-tech plans, and tolerates them for his wife's sake.

entries.group: Black Guard – High Lord Cassian Thorne
entries.question: Does the Flame Order suspect Cassian of anything?
entries.answer: They are indifferent to him.

entries.question: How do ordinary people come in contact with the spirit world?
entries.answer: It is disputed: kingdoms and peoples are divided over the answer (crossings, faint presence everywhere, human choices, omens), and the disagreement itself divides them.

entries.question: Who rules the Empire?
entries.answer: An Emperor with a Council of High Lords.

entries.question: Why is it called the Black Guard?
entries.answer: Cassian named it when he founded it from scratch: black like the night.

entries.question: Where is Book 1's first command?
entries.answer: The Desert Kingdom border. (Only the location is canon; the 'silent frontier / missing patrols / blaming spirit-humanoids' setup is draft, not canon, and the link to Rashid's war is not decided.)

entries.question: What's going on at the Desert Kingdom border when Book 1's first command begins?
entries.answer: The Desert Kingdom is preparing for another push from the enemy. The enemy armies have 2 paths they could take to get to the desert kingdom capital.

entries.question: Who is the enemy pushing toward the desert kingdom capital?
entries.answer: Both the unconquered part of the desert kingdom and a rival kingdom beyond the desert.

entries.question: Who holds the desert kingdom's capital right now?
entries.answer: The Empire holds the desert kingdom's capital.

entries.question: What are the two paths the enemy could take to the desert kingdom capital?
entries.answer: Path 1: a large canyon with a large desert crossing, with one major city. Path 2: the main roads with many fortified cities (seems like the more obvious way).

entries.question: Where is the Black Guard sent?
entries.answer: Alaric's Banner goes to the canyon; the others go to the cities.

entries.question: Which path does the enemy actually take?
entries.answer: The enemy takes the canyon, straight into Alaric's Banner.

entries.question: Does Alaric's Banner know the enemy is coming their way?
entries.answer: After studying maps, technology, enemy habits and previous war conduct, Alaric sees something can very likely happen. The High Lord also sees something, but the other commanders don't see it or don't see it as likely. Other Black Guard Banners want to be where they will be the most help; some Banner commanders are noble and want glory, some just feel they need to be smart about it and be where the enemy will be.

entries.question: Which High Lord also sees the canyon attack coming?
entries.answer: Cassian will see it but likes how Alaric is choosing it. Rashid sees something but is overruled by his confident advisors and division commanders.

entries.question: Does Alaric's Banner face the canyon attack alone?
entries.answer: The canyon city has a division.

entries.question: Whose division is in the canyon city?
entries.answer: The general is a desert kingdom general. 3/4 of his division is desert kingdom regiments and the rest are Imperial regiments, which this general favors.

entries.question: How do the general's desert regiments feel about him favoring the Imperial ones?
entries.answer: The desert regiments resent it, and morale is low.

entries.question: How does the canyon city's general treat Alaric's Banner when they arrive?
entries.answer: He sees them as outsiders meddling in his command, and he ignores Alaric's warning that the enemy will come through the canyon.

entries.question: With the general ignoring him, what does Alaric do?
entries.answer: He wins over the desert regiment he is under, and slowly the other desert regiments.

entries.question: How does Alaric win the desert regiments over?
entries.answer: He treats them as equals (unlike the general), learns their ways and language, and wins them with his recon and intelligence.

entries.question: When the enemy hits the canyon, how does the battle start?
entries.answer: All three: Alaric's preparations hold the first wave; the general is caught off guard and the city nearly falls; the enemy uses spirit-tech or something nobody expected.

entries.question: What's the unexpected thing the enemy brings to the canyon?
entries.answer: Spirit-heavy creatures or fighters, and tunnels or a hidden route through the canyon.

entries.question: Who finds the tunnels or hidden route?
entries.answer: Seraphina's recon, and desert soldiers who know the canyon tell Alaric about it.

entries.question: How does the canyon battle end?
entries.answer: They hold the city, but the general takes the credit. It's a costly win with heavy losses.

entries.question: Who knows the truth that Alaric really saved the canyon city?
entries.answer: The desert regiments and Cassian. Rashid somewhat knows, but he needs to keep the armies united.

entries.question: What does Cassian do with what he knows about Alaric saving the canyon city?
entries.answer: Cassian praises Alaric privately, pulls Alaric closer as his protégé, and uses Alaric's win to push his own ideas.

entries.question: How does Seraphina react to her father pulling Alaric closer?
entries.answer: She's proud of Alaric and happy for him, and a little uneasy but can't say why yet.

entries.question: What happens to the general who took the credit for the canyon?
entries.answer: The general is promoted or rewarded.

entries.question: What does the canyon fight reveal about the spirit-heavy creatures or fighters?
entries.answer: They found out there are such things as spirit creatures and that they can be used.

entries.question: Who learns that spirit creatures can be used?
entries.answer: Only Alaric, Seraphina and their Banner learn it, plus Cassian, who learns it and connects it to the spirit-tech power he's chasing.

entries.question: Does Cassian tell them to keep the spirit creatures secret?
entries.answer: No, they keep it quiet on their own.

entries.question: Why do Alaric, Seraphina and the Banner keep the spirit creatures quiet?
entries.answer: Because nobody would believe them, to avoid panic, and because they want to understand it before telling anyone.

entries.question: What do Alaric and Seraphina do next to understand the spirit creatures?
entries.answer: They can find dead ones, and they do try to question the Flame Order.

entries.question: How does the Flame Order respond when Alaric and Seraphina question them about the spirit creatures?
entries.answer: They are cautious and don't fully have answers, but a team of their members was there to help towards the end of the battle.

entries.question: How does the Flame Order team help near the end of the canyon battle?
entries.answer: They fight the spirit creatures directly.

entries.question: Why was a Flame Order team at the canyon at all?
entries.answer: They sensed the spirit creatures coming, and they were already tracking the enemy for their own reasons.

entries.question: What is the Flame Order's purpose (and its own reason for tracking the enemy)?
entries.answer: The Flame Order is to understand what is spirit, to hold the teaching of it, and to pass down traditions on how to handle spirits, especially with force.

entries.question: How do ordinary people see the Flame Order?
entries.answer: Like holders of the Empire's spiritual traditions.

entries.question: How does the Flame Order relate to the Emperor and the Council?
entries.answer: The Flame Order is independent and answers to no one.

entries.question: What happens between Alaric and the Flame Order team after the canyon?
entries.answer: They form a cautious alliance; they part ways but keep in touch.

entries.question: Where does Alaric's Banner go after the canyon?
entries.answer: Alaric's Banner is sent to a new front.

entries.question: Which front is Alaric's Banner sent to after the canyon?
entries.answer: The North-East Farm Kingdom, where the colony is being attacked by elves.

entries.question: Why are the elves attacking the Farm Kingdom colony?
entries.answer: The colony was built on land the elves see as theirs, and something is driving or corrupting the elves.

entries.question: Is Alaric's sister in danger when the Banner arrives in the Farm Kingdom?
entries.answer: The war is happening in the outskirts, though there are things that happen. (What happens is undecided.)

entries.question: What kind of weird things are happening in the Farm Kingdom?
entries.answer: Crops and animals are sickening or changing; people are vanishing near the forest; there are strange lights or sounds at night; and attacks.

entries.question: Who is behind the attacks in the Farm Kingdom?
entries.answer: The elves; spirit creatures, like the ones in the canyon; and unknown forces nobody can identify yet.

entries.question: How does Alaric first approach the Farm Kingdom problem?
entries.answer: He sends Seraphina's recon into the forest, talks to the farmers and his sister to learn what's happening, and tries to make contact with the elves.

entries.question: When Alaric tries to contact the elves, how do they respond?
entries.answer: Cant be found

entries.question: What does Seraphina's recon find in the forest?
entries.answer: Signs of the elves, but no elves. Dead or changed animals. Traces of spirit creatures. Some of the missing people.

entries.question: How is the Flame Order organized?
entries.answer: A strict ranked hierarchy.

entries.question: Who leads the Flame Order at the top?
entries.answer: A small circle leads it (not necessarily elders). Chumi doesn't care about the name; Story named it the Ember Circle (renamable).

entries.question: How does someone join the Flame Order?
entries.answer: Anyone can join if they pass trials. But the trials are vague and few pass, and joining them is not the life everyone wants to live.

entries.question: What makes the Flame Order life one most people don't want?
entries.answer: They give up family and home. Strict vows and discipline.

entries.question: What is a Black Guard Banner's main job in the Empire?
entries.answer: Both an elite force sent to the hardest fronts and Cassian's personal army, kinda like the airborne when they first started but with spirit instead of air.

entries.question: Spirit instead of air: how does the Black Guard use spirit?
entries.answer: Spirit-tech gear and weapons. Soldiers trained to sense or fight spirit. Spirit lets them move or strike in ways others can't.

entries.question: How does the Flame Order feel about the Black Guard using spirit this way?
entries.answer: They don't approve but don't stop it. They don't know how much the Guard uses. They trained some of the Guard themselves.

entries.question: How do regular Imperial soldiers see the Black Guard?
entries.answer: The same as the airborne.

entries.question: How does someone get into the Black Guard?
entries.answer: Volunteers who pass hard selection.

entries.question: Where do Black Guard volunteers come from?
entries.answer: From any kingdom in the Empire.

entries.question: What does the Black Guard selection test the most?
entries.answer: Physical endurance. Whether they can handle spirit. Loyalty and character.

entries.question: When a Black Guard soldier's loyalty is tested, who are they loyal to first?
entries.answer: The Emperor.

entries.question: The Guard is Cassian's army but loyal to the Emperor first. Does Cassian see that as a problem?
entries.answer: No, he's loyal to the Emperor too.

entries.question: How does the Emperor see the Black Guard?
entries.answer: As an experiment.

entries.question: What happens to the Black Guard if the experiment fails?
entries.answer: It gets disbanded. It's folded into the regular army. Cassian takes the fall.

entries.question: How many Banners does the Black Guard have when the story starts?
entries.answer: There can be 5 to 8 Banners.

entries.question: About how many soldiers are in one Black Guard Banner?
entries.answer: A few hundred, like a company or battalion.

entries.question: How is a Black Guard Banner split up inside?
entries.answer: Mainly infantry with recon and heavy support.

entries.question: Do the Black Guard Banners know about each other's missions?
entries.answer: They share up the chain of command and command delegates, and they know what others are delegated.

entries.question: Do the Banner commanders get along with each other?
entries.answer: There's a rivalry between the glory-seekers and the careful ones. One commander openly dislikes Alaric. They are also brothers in arms.

entries.question: Why does that commander openly dislike Alaric?
entries.answer: A glory-seeker who thinks Alaric is too cautious.

entries.question: Where is the Black Guard's home base?
entries.answer: A fortress of its own.

entries.question: What's the Black Guard's fortress called?
entries.answer: Chumi said 'You pick'; Story named it Nightwatch Keep (placeholder, renamable).

entries.question: Where is Nightwatch Keep?
entries.answer: Hidden Mountain range somewhere between the farm and desert kingdoms.

entries.question: Who knows where Nightwatch Keep is?
entries.answer: Only the Black Guard and Cassian. The Emperor and Council too. The Flame Order knows.

entries.question: What's inside Nightwatch Keep besides barracks?
entries.answer: Training grounds for the selection. Workshops where spirit-tech is made. Cassian's private rooms and secrets.

entries.question: Who makes the spirit-tech in the Keep's workshops?
entries.answer: Imperial engineers. Former Flame Order members. Craftsmen Cassian recruited himself.

entries.question: Why would Flame Order members leave the Order to work for the Guard?
entries.answer: They failed or quit the Order's strict life. They believe spirit should be used, not just guarded. Cassian pays or promises them a lot.

entries.question: Does the Flame Order know its former members work for the Guard?
entries.answer: Yes, and they resent it.

entries.question: Who rules the enemy kingdoms?
entries.answer: Each enemy kingdom has a different kind of ruler: one a warrior king, one a spirit queen or sorceress, one a council of warlords. (Tentative: Chumi said 'One of each maybe'.)

entries.question: Which kind of ruler leads the rival kingdom beyond the desert?
entries.answer: The warrior king.

entries.question: What does the warrior king want from the Desert Kingdom?
entries.answer: Land and resources. To push the Empire back out. Something spirit-related hidden there.

entries.question: Does the warrior king know about the spirit creatures his army used at the canyon?
entries.answer: Yes, he ordered their use. Someone else in his army brought them. He's being used by a hidden power.

entries.question: Who is the person in the warrior king's army who brought the spirit creatures?
entries.answer: A foreign advisor.

entries.question: Where does the foreign advisor come from?
entries.answer: Somewhere no one has heard of.

entries.question: Is the foreign advisor connected to the unknown forces attacking the Farm Kingdom?
entries.answer: Yes, they come from the same source.

entries.question: What does that shared source want?
entries.answer: To weaken the Empire from many sides. To spread corruption into the world. The same ancient device Cassian is chasing.

entries.question: Should the shared source have a name readers learn early, or stay unnamed for a while?
entries.answer: It stays unnamed for most of Book 1.

entries.question: Which enemy kingdom does the spirit queen or sorceress rule?
entries.answer: A kingdom not met yet in Book 1.

entries.question: And the council of warlords: where do readers meet them?
entries.answer: Southern kingdoms. And mountain kingdoms.

entries.question: Are the southern and mountain kingdoms at war with the Empire during Book 1?
entries.answer: Yes, open war. But like the 100 years war.

entries.question: How did Alaric end up in the Black Guard?
entries.answer: He volunteered and passed selection like everyone else.

entries.question: What was Alaric before he volunteered?
entries.answer: A regular Imperial soldier. A farmer's son.

entries.question: Why did Alaric volunteer for the Black Guard?
entries.answer: To make a bigger difference in the war.

entries.question: How long was Alaric a regular soldier before he volunteered?
entries.answer: 4 or 5 years.

entries.question: What did Alaric see or do as a soldier that made him want a bigger role?
entries.answer: The Black Guard wasn't a thing before him. But he saw it as the best of the best.

entries.question: Alaric's younger brother
entries.answer: He and his younger brother became officers, but his brother was happy where he stayed.

entries.question: Since the Black Guard was new, was Alaric in its very first selection class?
entries.answer: He was in one of the first few classes.

entries.question: How do Alaric and his younger brother get along now?
entries.answer: Very close but forget to communicate to each other.

entries.question: How big was the Black Guard's first selection class?
entries.answer: The first "class" was a division size.

entries.question: How did a division-sized first class end up as just a few Banners?
entries.answer: 2 to 3 banners is a regiment, a few regiments is a division. But since it is just one division there are no formal regiments, since the Black Guard is spread out. The next "class" is bigger and maybe getting more formal.

entries.question: When does the bigger next selection class happen?
entries.answer: As they finish training the first class, the next class is already starting training.

entries.question: Who trains the new class while the first class is out fighting?
entries.answer: All: veterans from the first class rotate back to train them; former Flame Order members at Nightwatch Keep train them; Imperial army instructors train them.

entries.question: Does Alaric ever rotate back to Nightwatch Keep to train recruits?
entries.answer: No, he stays at the front.

entries.question: Where is Alaric's younger brother serving when Book 1 starts?
entries.answer: In the regular army on another front. But: I guess it's worth exploring that maybe you have to join your local kingdom's army then transfer to the Imperial, and both him and his brother went all the way to the Imperial army.

entries.question: How do soldiers get into the Imperial army?
entries.answer: Worth exploring (tentative): maybe you have to join your local kingdom's army, then transfer to the Imperial army.

entries.question: What does it take to transfer from a kingdom's army to the Imperial army?
entries.answer: Years of service and a good record. You have to pass a test or trial.

entries.question: Which kingdom's army did Alaric and his brother start in?
entries.answer: The Farm Kingdom's army.

entries.question: Why did Alaric and his brother join the Farm Kingdom's army in the first place?
entries.answer: Kingdom needed more soldiers and their father died as a drafted officer.

entries.question: Who runs the family farm now that the father is gone and both sons are soldiers?
entries.answer: Brother-in-law, sister and mom took over.

entries.question: How many sisters does Alaric have?
entries.answer: Two sisters: one runs the farm with her husband, the other is married to the Capital High Lord.

entries.question: Besides the younger brother, does Alaric also have an older brother in the Flame Order?
entries.answer: Yes, he has an older brother in the Flame Order and a younger brother in the army.

entries.question: How did a farmer's son (Alaric's older brother) end up joining the Flame Order?
entries.answer: He passed the trials as a young man. He felt called to it.

entries.question: Since Flame Order members give up family and home, how does the older brother relate to Alaric now?
entries.answer: They rarely speak; he's distant, but he still wants to know how the family is doing. It's more like he is busy and needs to be away. He is cautious about the Black Guard but doesn't fully understand it.

entries.question: Does Alaric's older brother show up in Book 1?
entries.answer: Yes, but somewhere else in the story (not on the canyon Flame team).

entries.question: Is Alaric's mom still living on the family farm?
entries.answer: Yes, she still lives on the farm.

entries.question: How did the other sister, a farmer's daughter, come to marry the Capital High Lord?
entries.answer: They met by chance and fell in love. She earned her own place in the Capital first.

entries.question: Some pages call him "Sir Alaric." Does a farmer's son get that title?
entries.answer: Sir could be an officer term. (Tentative)

entries.question: Which southern and mountain kingdoms are at war with the Empire?
entries.answer: Rival kingdoms beyond the Empire's southern and mountain borders, not Davian's or Bjorn's.

entries.question: Whose soldiers mostly fight the rival kingdoms at the southern and mountain borders?
entries.answer: Both together (Davian's and Bjorn's own kingdom armies and the Imperial army).

entries.question: Which front is Alaric's younger brother on?
entries.answer: The southern border.

entries.question: What's the younger brother's name?
entries.answer: You pick. Story picked Rowan Vaelen (placeholder, renamable).

entries.question: What's Rowan's rank on the southern border?
entries.answer: A junior officer.
